PG Funding: PhD Studentship - Process Industries: Net Zero CDT: Sustainable, High-resolution Purification of GLP-1 Peptide Therapeutics

Newcastle University

Qualification Type: PhD
Location: Newcastle upon Tyne
Funding for: UK Students
Funding amount: £21,805 - please see advert
Hours: Full Time
Placed On: 19th November 2026
Closes: 27th January 2027
Reference: PINZ06-27

Award summary

100% fees (UK Home only), a minimum tax-free annual living allowance at 2027/28 UKRI Rate (UKRI 2026/7 Rate: £21,805), and a research training support grant of £20,000.

Overview

This PhD project is part of the EPSRC Process Industries: Net Zero (PINZ) Centre for Doctoral Training and will be supported by Sunresin Life Sciences. 

GLP-1 receptor agonists such as semaglutide and tirzepatide are among the fastest-growing peptide drugs, but manufacturing capacity is struggling to keep pace with demand. Purification is the main bottleneck. These peptides are long, hydrophobic and prone to aggregation, so reversed-phase chromatography consumes large volumes of solvent, mostly acetonitrile, and generates much of the process waste. This 4-year PhD project in partnership with Sunresin Life Sciences will develop more efficient and sustainable purification processes for GLP-1 peptides, using the industrial partner’s Seplife LXU (pure silica) and LXX (hybrid silica) media. The student will first synthesise GLP-1 analogues and then systematically screen stationary phase chemistry, particle size, pH, temperature and mobile phase composition. The LXX phases are of particular interest because their wide pH and temperature tolerance allows high-pH and high-aqueous separations that can reduce acetonitrile use and improve resolution of closely related impurities. 

The project will measure the benefits using green metrics such as process mass intensity and solvent consumption per gram of purified peptide and will scale the best methods up from analytical to preparative level, including dual-column and continuous approaches. This aligns directly with the PINZ (Process Industries Net Zero) CDT’s aim of cutting solvent use, waste and energy demand in pharmaceutical manufacturing. By working closely with industrial partners and applying advanced chromatography approaches, the student will help shape more sustainable manufacturing routes for life-changing medicines while gaining experience at the interface of academic research and industrial innovation. 

Number of awards: 1

Start date: 1st October 2027

Award duration: 4 years

Sponsor: EPSRC

Supervisors

Dr. Othman Al Musaimi (Othman.Almusaimi@newcastle.ac.uk)

Eligibility criteria

You must have, or expect to gain, a minimum 2:1 Honours degree or international equivalent in a subject relevant to the proposed PhD project. Due to nature of this project, the candidate should have a strong background in Engineering, especially Chemical Engineering, Analytical Chemistry, Peptide Chemistry, or another closely related engineering subject. Enthusiasm for research, the ability to think and work independently, excellent analytical skills and strong verbal and written communication skills are also essential requirements.

This studentship is available to UK Home students only.

How to apply

You must apply through the University’s Apply to Newcastle Portal. Once registered select ‘Create a Postgraduate Application’.

Identify your programme of study via ‘Course Search’

  • Search for the ‘Course Title’ using the programme code: 8856F
  • Leave the 'Research Area' field blank
  • Select ‘PhD in Process Industries; Net Zero (PINZ)' as the programme of study

You will then need to provide the following information in the ‘Further Details’ section:

  • Personal Statement (mandatory): Upload a document or write a statement directly into the application form
  • Studentship/Partnership Reference: Enter the studentship code: PINZ06-27
  • Research Proposal: When asked how you are providing your research proposal, select ‘Write Proposal’, and enter the research project from this advert. You do not need to upload a separate research proposal.
  • Supporting documents: Upload your CV

You must submit one application per studentship. You cannot apply for multiple studentships in one application.

Contact details

General enquiries: pinz.cdt@ncl.ac.uk
